slot.brief: Two bodies thrown/projected (e.g. one from a cliff, another upward) meet after a given time; set up two equations and solve for the unknown speed or time.

stem: A body is projected vertically upward from the ground at $20$ m s$^{-1}$. At the same instant, another body is projected vertically downward from a point $100$ m above the ground. They meet after $2$ s. Find the initial speed of the second body. Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: After 2 s, the first body is at height 20(2) − ½(10)(2²) = 20 m. For the second body to be there, 100 − 2u − 20 = 20, giving u = 30 m s⁻¹.

working:
At $t=2$ s, first body's height: $y_1=20(2)-\dfrac{1}{2}(10)(2)^2=20$ m.
Second body's height: $y_2=100-u(2)-\dfrac{1}{2}(10)(2)^2$.
$y_1=y_2\Rightarrow20=80-2u\Rightarrow u=30$ m s$^{-1}$

Independent check: After 2 s, the first body is at height 20(2) − ½(10)(2²) = 20 m. For the second body to be there, 100 − 2u − 20 = 20, giving u = 30 m s⁻¹.
solution:
Taking upward as positive, after $2$ s the first body is at height
$$y_1=20(2)-\frac12(10)(2)^2=20\text{ m}.$$
For the second body, $y_2=100-2u-\frac12(10)(2)^2$. Equating heights gives $20=80-2u$, hence $u=30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. (A)
